transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I came in because I’m just tired all the time. By midmorning at work, even if I’ve only been reviewing files or helping a junior adjuster with a claim, I feel like my body and my brain are already running on empty.
Do you have trouble falling asleep at night, or do you wake up frequently once you're asleep?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t paid close attention to whether I’m waking up a lot or having trouble falling asleep. I just know I don’t feel rested.
Do you feel unrefreshed when you wake up, even if you think you’ve slept long enough?

Yeah, I think so. Even when it seems like I got enough sleep, I still wake up feeling worn out. And by midmorning at work, even if I’m just reviewing files or helping someone with a claim, I already feel like I’m running on empty.
Have you noticed yourself feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?

Yes. Most days I feel kind of down, like there’s a gray film over everything. Even when my husband is being kind, or we’re cooking with the family, I can go through the motions, but I don’t really feel the enjoyment from it the way I used to.
Have you noticed a decrease in your energy levels or an increase in fatigue, even when you haven’t done anything physically or mentally demanding?

Yes. That’s actually a big part of why I came in. I’m tired all the time. By midmorning at work, even if I’ve only been reviewing files or walking a junior adjuster through a claim, it feels like my body and my brain are already running on empty.
Have you noticed yourself moving more slowly than usual, or feeling restless and unable to sit still?
I’m not sure I’ve noticed that, honestly. I don’t think I’m especially restless or pacing around. Moving slower… maybe sometimes, but I can’t really say for sure.
Do you find yourself sleeping longer than usual at night, or needing to take naps during the day?
I’m not really sure. I don’t think I’m sleeping a lot longer than usual, and I don’t usually nap during the day. I just feel tired, but the sleep part… I haven’t noticed a clear change.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight lately, like eating less than usual or losing weight without trying?
I haven’t really noticed a big change there. My appetite seems about the same, and I don’t think I’ve lost weight without trying.
Can you think back and tell me if you usually have trouble falling asleep at night, or if you wake up during the night and have difficulty going back to sleep?
I’m not really sure. I don’t think I have a regular problem with falling asleep, and I can’t say I’m up a lot in the night unable to get back to sleep. Nothing that stands out to me.
Do you ever find yourself dozing off or falling asleep during the day, even when you’re trying to stay awake, like during meetings or while driving?
No, I don’t think so. I might feel tired during the day, but I’m not actually nodding off in meetings or while driving.
Even though you don’t fall asleep during the day, do you feel a strong need to sleep or an overwhelming urge to nap during the day?
Not really, no. I might feel worn out sometimes, but I don’t feel like I have this overwhelming urge to nap during the day.
Do you ever feel like you could fall asleep easily during the day, even in quiet or boring situations, like sitting at your desk or watching TV?
I haven’t really noticed that, no. If I’m sitting quietly or watching TV I might feel tired, but I don’t think I’m just ready to fall asleep easily.

Even if you don’t feel like you’re about to fall asleep, do you feel unusually sleepy during the day—like you’re struggling to stay alert even when you’re trying to focus, such as during work or a conversation?

Yeah, I’d say it’s more like being worn down than sleepy. I came in because I’m tired all the time. By midmorning at work, even just reviewing claim files or walking a junior adjuster through something, it feels like my body and my brain are already running on empty.
Even when you feel like you’ve gotten enough sleep, do you still wake up feeling unrested or like you didn’t truly rest?

Yeah. Even if I think I slept enough, I don’t really wake up feeling restored. It’s like I start the day already tired, and by midmorning at work, just going through files or helping someone with a claim, my body and my brain feel like they’re already running on empty.
Do you find that you don’t take pleasure in things you used to enjoy, like hobbies, time with family, or other activities?

Yes. Most days it feels like there’s kind of a gray film over everything. Even when my husband is being kind, or we’re cooking with the family, I can go through the motions, but I don’t really feel the enjoyment from it the way I used to.
Do you ever have trouble staying awake during passive activities, like reading, watching TV, or sitting quietly without much stimulation?
I don’t know that I’d say I’m actually dozing off during those things. I can feel drained or kind of checked out, but I haven’t really noticed myself falling asleep just from reading or watching TV.
Have you ever found yourself suddenly falling asleep or struggling to stay awake in situations where you need to stay alert, like during important conversations, while working, or in meetings?
No, I don’t think so. I mean, I feel tired at work or in conversations sometimes, but I’m not suddenly falling asleep or fighting to keep my eyes open in a meeting or anything like that.
Do you ever struggle to stay awake during active tasks that require your attention, like working on a project, having a conversation, or doing something that normally interests you?
Not really. I can feel worn out or distracted, but I don’t usually feel like I’m about to fall asleep when I’m working on something or talking with someone.
Can you recall if your tiredness tends to get worse on days when your sleep felt lighter, more broken, or less restful?

I’m not sure it’s only tied to how I slept. I came in because I’m tired all the time. Even by midmorning at work, after reviewing files or walking a junior adjuster through a claim, I feel like my body and my brain are already running on empty.
